lessons.summary: Greet your neighbour the Hong Kong way and hear your first tones.

content.title: Hello and the six tones
content.scenario: Greet your neighbour the Hong Kong way and hear your first tones.

rounds.situation: You bump into your neighbour by the lift in the morning.
rounds.jyutping: zou2 san4

chunks.note: Hong Kong’s morning greeting, used until about noon. 早 zou2 rises, 晨 san4 falls low: your first two tones.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Greet your neighbour in the morning.

rounds.situation: They smile back, so keep it friendly.
rounds.jyutping: nei5 hou2 aa3

chunks.note: 呀 at the end makes 你好 sound warm instead of stiff.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say a warm hello.

rounds.situation: Your neighbour asks the classic Cantonese check-in.
rounds.jyutping: sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3

chunks.note: Not really about food: it is how people say “how are you?”.
Keeps the question gentle and caring.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask your neighbour if they have eaten yet.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3

rounds.situation: Answer and thank them for asking.
rounds.jyutping: sik6 zo2 laa3 do1 ze6

chunks.note: 喇 marks that something has now happened.
多謝 is for kindness or gifts; 唔該 is for a service. 多 do1 is high and flat, 謝 ze6 is low and flat.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you’ve eaten and thank them.

rounds.situation: The lift arrives. Say goodbye.
rounds.jyutping: baai1 baai3 haa6 ci3 gin3

chunks.note: Everyone in Hong Kong says it, from kids to grandparents.
A friendly way to close any chat.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say goodbye and see you next time.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: baai1 baai3 haa6 ci3 gin3

lessons.summary: Introduce yourself at a friend’s party in a few easy lines.

content.title: Who I am
content.scenario: Introduce yourself at a friend’s party in a few easy lines.

rounds.situation: At a party, someone new turns to you.
rounds.jyutping: nei5 giu3 me1 meng2 aa3

chunks.note: Literally “you are called what name?”. 名 is said meng2 in speech.
Makes a direct question sound friendly.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask someone their name.

rounds.situation: Tell them your name.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 giu3 Alex

chunks.note: Just add your own name after 我叫.
English names are completely normal in Hong Kong.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say your own name.

rounds.situation: They ask where you’re from.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 hai6 mei5 gwok3 jan4

chunks.note: 係 links you to what you are.
Swap in your country + 人: 英國人, 加拿大人, 澳洲人.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say where you’re from.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: ngo5 hai6 mei5 gwok3 jan4

rounds.situation: They’re impressed you speak a little.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 sik1 siu2 siu2 gwong2 dung1 waa2

chunks.note: Modest and charming: locals love hearing this.
話 is said waa2 here, with a rising tone.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you know a little Cantonese.

rounds.situation: Wrap up the chat warmly.
rounds.jyutping: hou2 hoi1 sam1 sik1 dou2 nei5

chunks.note: 好 before a feeling means “really”.
識到 is getting to know someone new.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell them it’s nice to meet them.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: hou2 hoi1 sam1 sik1 dou2 nei5

lessons.summary: Visit Grandma and introduce someone special.

content.title: Meet the family
content.scenario: Visit Grandma and introduce someone special.

rounds.situation: You arrive at Grandma’s flat for Sunday lunch.
rounds.jyutping: maa4 maa4 zou2 san4

chunks.note: Your dad’s mum. Your mum’s mum is 婆婆 po4 po2.
Always greet elders first when you walk in.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Greet Grandma as you arrive.

rounds.situation: Introduce the person standing next to you.
rounds.jyutping: ni1 go3 hai6 ngo5 naam4 pang4 jau5

chunks.note: Point and introduce anyone with 呢個係.
Swap in 女朋友 (girlfriend), 老公 (husband) or 老婆 (wife).

rounds.speakingPrompt: Introduce your partner to Grandma.

rounds.situation: Win Grandma over with a compliment.
rounds.jyutping: keoi5 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 nei5 zyu2 ge3 sung3

chunks.note: 佢 means both he and she.
餸 is home-cooked dishes. The fastest way to Grandma’s heart.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell Grandma your partner loves her cooking.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: keoi5 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 nei5 zyu2 ge3 sung3

options.englishTranslation: Mum and Dad really miss you.

rounds.situation: Pass on a message from your parents.
rounds.jyutping: baa4 baa1 maa4 maa1 dou1 hou2 gwaa3 zyu6 nei5
rounds.translation: Mum and Dad really miss you.

chunks.note: 都 groups people together: “both / all”.
掛住 is missing someone you love.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell Grandma your parents miss her.

rounds.situation: Time to leave. Show you care.
rounds.jyutping: maa4 maa4 nei5 jiu3 bou2 zung6 san1 tai2 aa3
rounds.translation: Grandma, take care of your health.

chunks.jyutping: nei5 jiu3 bou2 zung6 san1 tai2
chunks.note: The classic loving goodbye to an elder.
Adds warmth so it sounds caring, not bossy.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say a caring goodbye to Grandma.

responseExercise.promptTranslation: Grandma, take care of your health.

lessons.summary: Buy fish balls from a street stall and pay like a local.

content.title: Numbers and money
content.scenario: Buy fish balls from a street stall and pay like a local.

rounds.situation: A street stall smells amazing. Order a snack.
rounds.jyutping: jat1 cyun3 jyu4 daan2

chunks.note: 串 counts things on a stick.
Hong Kong’s most famous street snack.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Order one skewer of fish balls.

rounds.situation: Ask the price before you pay.
rounds.jyutping: gei2 do1 cin2 aa3

chunks.note: The one question you’ll use every single day.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask how much it costs.

rounds.situation: The vendor answers.
rounds.jyutping: sap6 ji6 man1

chunks.note: Numbers stack simply: 十 (ten) + 二 (two).
Everyday word for Hong Kong dollars. It also means mosquito!

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say the price: twelve dollars.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: sap6 ji6 man1

rounds.situation: They’re so good you want more.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 jiu3 loeng5 cyun3

chunks.note: Simple and direct is normal at a stall.
Use 兩, not 二, when counting things.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Order two skewers.

rounds.situation: Ask if you can tap your card.
rounds.jyutping: paak3 baat3 daat6 tung1 dak1 m4 dak1

chunks.note: The Octopus card pays for almost everything in Hong Kong.
Add it after any request to ask permission.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask if you can pay with your Octopus card.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: paak3 baat3 daat6 tung1 dak1 m4 dak1

lessons.summary: Order an iced lemon tea and a pineapple bun your way.

content.title: Cha chaan teng order
content.scenario: Order an iced lemon tea and a pineapple bun your way.

rounds.situation: You sit down and wave to the waiter.
rounds.jyutping: m4 goi1 ngo5 soeng2 giu3 je5
rounds.translation: Excuse me, I’d like to order.

chunks.note: Use 唔該 to get attention or thank someone for a service.
叫嘢 literally means “call things”: it is how locals say order.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Call the waiter over and say you want to order.

rounds.situation: The waiter is ready. Ask for the classic drink.
rounds.jyutping: jiu3 jat1 bui1 dung3 ning2 caa4

chunks.note: Start any order with 要 plus the amount.
Hong Kong’s favourite drink. 凍 means iced.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Order one iced lemon tea.

rounds.situation: Make the drink exactly how you like it.
rounds.jyutping: siu2 tim4 zau2 bing1

chunks.note: 少 + a taste asks for less of it.
走 means “leave out”: 走冰 is no ice.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask for your drink less sweet and with no ice.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: siu2 tim4 zau2 bing1

rounds.situation: Add something to eat with your tea.
rounds.jyutping: zoi3 jiu3 jat1 go3 bo1 lo4 jau4
rounds.translation: And a pineapple bun with butter, too.

chunks.note: 再要 adds another item to your order.
No pineapple inside: the crust just looks like one.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Add a pineapple bun to your order.

rounds.situation: You’re done. Ask for the bill.
rounds.jyutping: m4 goi1 maai4 daan1

chunks.note: Same 唔該 as before: polite and quick.
埋單 is what everyone says to pay up.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Get the waiter’s attention and ask for the bill.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: m4 goi1 maai4 daan1

And a pineapple bun with butter, too.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask how many people (as the host would).

rounds.situation: Tell them your group size.

chunks.note: Number + 位 is the polite way to count people.
Tag it on the end for a service.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Order a pot of pu’er.

rounds.jyutping: jiu3 jat1 lung4 haa1 gaau2 tung4 siu1 maai2

lessons.summary: Take a taxi across town and get dropped off where you want.

content.title: Getting around
content.scenario: Take a taxi across town and get dropped off where you want.

rounds.situation: You jump into a red taxi.
rounds.jyutping: si1 fu2 heoi3 zim1 saa1 zeoi2 m4 goi1
rounds.translation: Driver, to Tsim Sha Tsui, please.

chunks.note: Respectful way to address drivers and tradespeople.
去 + place is all you need.
Polite and short.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell the driver where to go.

rounds.situation: Near the area, the driver asks you.
rounds.jyutping: hai2 bin1 dou6 lok6 ce1 aa3
rounds.translation: Where do you want to get out?

chunks.note: 邊度 means where; 喺 means at.
落 means get off: 落車, 落船, 落樓.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask where to get out (as the driver would).

rounds.situation: Point ahead.
rounds.jyutping: cin4 min6 jau5 lok6

chunks.note: The famous minibus phrase. It works in taxis too.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask to be dropped off up ahead.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: cin4 min6 jau5 lok6

options.englishTranslation: Where do you want to get out?

rounds.situation: You see your spot.
rounds.jyutping: ni1 dou6 ting4 zau6 dak1 laa3

chunks.note: 呢度 means here.
Signals “that works, we’re done”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell the driver to stop here.

rounds.situation: Pay and be generous.
rounds.jyutping: m4 sai2 zaau2 laa3 do1 ze6

chunks.note: 唔使 means “no need”.
多謝 for the kindness of a good ride.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell the driver to keep the change.

lessons.summary: Talk food with a friend and pick where to eat.

content.title: Likes and dislikes
content.scenario: Talk food with a friend and pick where to eat.

rounds.situation: A friend is planning dinner.
rounds.jyutping: nei5 zung1 m4 zung1 ji3 sik6 laat6

chunks.note: Cantonese asks yes/no questions as “like-not-like”.
辣 is spicy.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask your friend if they like spicy food.

rounds.situation: You love it.
rounds.jyutping: zung1 ji3 aa3 jyut6 laat6 jyut6 hou2
rounds.translation: I do, the spicier the better!

chunks.note: Answer by repeating the verb: no need for “yes”.
越…越… means “the more…the more…”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you love spicy food.

rounds.situation: But there’s one thing you can’t stand.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 m4 zung1 ji3 sik6 lau4 lin4

chunks.note: 唔 in front makes anything negative.
The king of fruits. People love it or hate it.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say one food you don’t like.

options.englishTranslation: I do, the spicier the better!

rounds.situation: Explain why.

chunks.note: Say it with feeling: 呀 makes it an exclamation.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say it smells terrible.

rounds.situation: Your friend has the answer.
rounds.jyutping: gam2 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 sik6 fo2 wo1 laa1

chunks.note: 咁 picks up from what was just said.
啦 turns it into a friendly suggestion.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Suggest going for hotpot.

lessons.summary: Buy fruit at the wet market and get a better deal.

content.title: Market shopping
content.scenario: Buy fruit at the wet market and get a better deal.

rounds.situation: At the wet market, oranges look perfect.
rounds.jyutping: lou5 baan2 di1 caang2 dim2 maai6 aa3
rounds.translation: Boss, how much are the oranges?

chunks.note: Call any stall owner 老闆. They like it.
啲 points to a group of things.
Literally “how do you sell?”: the market way to ask price.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask the stall owner how much the oranges are.

rounds.situation: The owner answers.
rounds.jyutping: sap6 man1 saam1 go3

chunks.note: Price first, then the amount you get.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say three for ten dollars (as the owner would).

rounds.situation: Try your luck.
rounds.jyutping: jau5 mou5 peng4 di1 aa3

chunks.note: 有冇 asks whether something exists: have or not.
啲 after a word means “a bit more”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask for a better price.

rounds.situation: The owner gives a little.
rounds.jyutping: ji6 sap6 man1 cat1 go3 laa1

chunks.note: Bigger deal, same pattern.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Make the counter-offer (as the owner would).

rounds.situation: Deal! Thank the owner.
rounds.jyutping: hou2 aa3 do1 ze6 lou5 baan2

chunks.note: Happy agreement.
多謝 because they did you a favour. Expect a free spring onion next time.
